transcript:
HEADER
Date: 2026-03-31
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~63 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel, June Park, Ethan Brooks, Maya Thompson, Priya Nair, Liam O'Connor + all squads on stream

SUMMARY (auto): Quick sync to review outcomes from last week's resilience-focused hackday. Leadership shares immediate commits and assigns owners. Open Q&A with some cross-talk.

TOPICS: hackday outcomes; on-call; culture commits; hiring runway; Q&A

[00:00] Samir Patel: Good morning everyone, uh thanks for joining. I want to start — quick context — last week we did the resilience hackday, and we asked teams to look for low-risk, high-impact fixes. Today is to surface those and make commitments. We'll keep it tight.

[00:22] June Park: Yep, thanks Samir. I'll kick off with product-level themes: persistence of KV cache misses, a few model routing fallbacks that were flaky under burst, and some small UX telem we should track. Not all of these are dramat — like real drama — but they add up.

[00:45] Maya Thompson: On the engineering side, most squads delivered small prototypes. We found an autoscaler edge case where if a large batch of short requests hit node spin-up, the backoff loop doubled latency. We have a patch that reduces churn.

[01:10] Ethan Brooks: To add — a couple teams worked on prefix KV cache heuristics; results are mixed but promising. Note: the transcription in the raw hackday notes sometimes says "K V cash" which is confusing but it's KV cache.

[01:38] Priya Nair: Our research crew also ran light evals on quantized variants under load; saw a small quality delta at tail latencies but major cost wins. We'll share a short note.

[02:05] Liam O'Connor: Ops observed that our current on-call rota gaps are real during EU mornings; hackday created a quick library to standardize runbook templates. We should adopt this across squads.

[02:30] Samir Patel: Good. Let's do commitments: two-week cadence of shipping the highest confidence fixes. Maya, can you take the autoscaler hotfix?

[02:45] Maya Thompson: Yeah I can own it, we'll need a quick e2e repro. I think we can get a hotfix in the next sprint.

[03:10] June Park: Also commit to rotating cross-squad demos every other week — we want more visibility into infra changes that affect latency/cost. That helps reduce surprise regressions.

[03:35] Audience (mic open): quick question — will these changes affect pricing or SLAs?

[03:45] Samir Patel: No spot changes to pricing; these are internal resilience and on-call improvements. SLA upgrades are separate and will need product+sales coordination.

[04:05] Unidentified Speaker: there's a note about fallback model variants doing silent failure — can we get an owner?

[04:20] Ethan Brooks: I'll take that with the runtime team. Might be related to kernel selection mismatches under long sequences. We'll run a small benchmark.

[04:50] Priya Nair: The eval doc will include the prompt sets we used; caveat, some model names got munged in the transcript — e.g., "Redwood-optim" got written as "read wood opt" — ignore typos.

[05:15] Samir Patel: Thanks. On culture: we heard feedback last quarter about psychological safety during on-call postmortems. June?

[05:28] June Park: Right. Action: mandate a blameless template for incident writes and encourage a 15-minute retro slot in squad meetings. People ops is on board. We also want to trial rotating demo presenters to build cross-polination.

[05:55] Maya Thompson: Small note — some folks flagged that the hackday timing clashed with customer SRE shifts; next time we should avoid EU peak windows.

[06:10] Liam O'Connor: We'll add a scheduling guardrail. Also, hiring update: we're projecting runway for next 4 months with current offers, but we need to speed up backend infra hiring. People ops will follow up.

[06:35] Audience (mic): are we prioritizing on-call tooling vs. latency optimizations?

[06:45] Samir Patel: Both — prioritize the things that lower operational toil first because they compound. Latency wins are still high value but often heavier lift.

[07:05] Unidentified Speaker: regarding the autoscaler repro — is there a public gist or doc?

[07:15] Maya Thompson: There's a doc in the hackday folder; I'll link it in #all-hands-docs. Expect an initial PR by next week.

[07:40] June Park: Scheduling: we'll circulate the cross-squad demo calendar today; please sign up.

[08:05] Priya Nair: On model evals — small ask: SEs, please review the quick eval results and flag any regressions. We don't want to silently accept tail-case quality drops for cost wins.

[08:30] Ethan Brooks: A technical deep dive on the autoscaler, batching heuristics, and kernel picks is scheduled next Tuesday; invites are going out.

[08:50] Audience (quick chorus): mm-hmm, sounds good, thanks.

[09:10] Samir Patel: Ok let's do a short open Q&A. We have about 50 minutes left; please keep questions high-signal.

[09:30] Unidentified Speaker 2: Will the on-call template include RACI for small teams?

[09:38] Liam O'Connor: Yes, the template defines RACI, escalation path, and a quick checklist. We'll pilot with three squads.

[10:05] Unidentified Speaker 3: Any blockers to rolling the autoscaler patch to dedicated clusters?

[10:12] Maya Thompson: Need a brief soak on staging and a load test; ops will coordinate. No fundamental blockers.

[10:40] June Park: People Ops note — hiring pipeline: aim to close 4 infra hires by end of Q2. We'll share targets.

[11:05] Samir Patel: Good. One more cultural ask: everyone please try to post a 2-line postmortem highlight in #incidents within 48 hours; short is okay, helps knowledge spread.

[11:28] Unidentified Speaker: Are we tracking rollback metrics centrally?

[11:35] Ethan Brooks: Not yet centrally; we should add to the console metrics. I'll put an issue.

[12:00] Audience (low): applause.

[12:25] Samir Patel: Wrap-up: commitments were made, owners assigned. We'll publish a doc with action items. Quick readout: autoscaler hotfix (Maya), on-call rota/runbook (Liam), demo rota (June), KV cache eval (Priya). Any objections?

[12:50] No objection heard.

[13:05] Samir Patel: Great, thank you. We'll follow up with invites for the technical deep dive. Meeting adjourned.

ACTION ITEMS (auto):
- Maya Thompson: Ship autoscaler hotfix; produce e2e repro; due 2026-04-13
- Liam O'Connor: Draft on-call rota and runbook; due 2026-04-07
- June Park: Coordinate rotating demos and publish calendar; due 2026-04-10
- Priya Nair: Publish KV cache heuristic eval; due 2026-04-14

END OF TRANSCRIPT
